sonnet.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine reads the same usage events and writes its invoices to the shadow store only.
sonnet.q2: The new engine computes, charges and writes the ledger. The old engine computes every invoice into the shadow store, never charges, and so stays current.
sonnet.q3: Gate A must be met: 7 consecutive days with a mismatch rate under 0.1%, and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person promotes, one step at a time.
sonnet.q4: A new-engine charge failure rate above 2% over any 10-minute window. It applies in `both`, and in `new_only` before day 35. Errors in `shadow` never trigger rollback.
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in `old_only`, with the gates reset. To take over again, the rollout must go through `shadow` again, and the 7-day count starts over.
sonnet.q6: It stops at day 35 in `new_only`. The usage event log keeps events only 35 days, so the earliest skipped events would be gone and the old engine could not reprocess them.
sonnet.q8: Evidence: the nightly comparison results, kept next to the shadow store, hold the daily mismatch rate and invoice counts. Finance sign-off is a recorded approval. The controller refuses a promotion whose gate is not met.
sonnet.q9: NOT STATED. The document names a "controller" only for refusing promotions. It does not say which component detects the rollback condition. It says the measured quantity is the new engine's charge failure rate, above 2% over any 10-minute window, and that rollback then starts automatically.
sonnet.q10: New charges are halted. Due charges are delayed, never dropped. In ResumeOldCharging, the old engine charges every due period that has no recorded charge.
sonnet.q11: ReconcileCharges treats the billing ledger as the list of charge keys already charged. A charge key is a customer plus a billing period, and an engine skips any key that already has a charge. ResumeOldCharging therefore skips periods the new engine already charged.
sonnet.q12: The rollback goes to `RollbackStuck` and pages on-call. The mode is not yet `old_only`, and new charges stay halted. Due charges are delayed, not dropped. On-call retries from the failed step, and every step is safe to re-run because it is keyed by charge key.
